description: Disk listings normalize relative paths to NFC before cataloging them. A Linux-mounted file such as Décembre-2020.md (decomposed e + combining acute) is visible in the Ingestion UI, but preview materialization and deletion resolve the composed path and fail with :enoent. Add regression coverage for list -> materialize/delete using the returned stable identity, preserve exact filesystem path spelling while retaining canonical logical identity and authorization/traversal boundaries, and cover normalization collisions safely. Action reuse assessment: extend the existing Storage/FileExplorer, EntryCatalog, materialize_document, and delete_document operations; no new Action or agent-tool exposure. Inputs/outputs/errors and NodeRouter boundaries remain unchanged. Verify through Storage public contracts, materializer integration, Unicode/property cases, focused tests, mix q, and required ingestion E2E where available.

comments.text: Implemented shared Storage path resolution for canonical Unicode equivalence. NFC logical/catalog paths now resolve segment-by-segment to exact filesystem spellings; multiple canonically equivalent siblings return :ambiguous_unicode_path instead of selecting one. Added regression coverage for Décembre-2020.md list -> materialize -> delete, pure equivalence/collision properties, and filesystem round-trip properties for Arabic, Chinese/CJK, Japanese, Devanagari, and Cyrillic filenames. Validation: 241 focused tests / 13 properties pass; mix q passes; ingestion E2E 9 passed / 3 skipped. Final mix precommit ran 9,080 tests and failed only four unrelated distributed peer-node tests with :peer_connection_failed; isolated rerun of those four failed identically. Context Mode also produced disk-I/O wrapper failures during precommit capture, so the final run used the documented filtered shell fallback. Work remains uncommitted for human review.

title: Fix decomposed Unicode disk document paths
